name: Design r: recursive discovery inside acquisition, with the discoverer amortised across categories
core_idea: Move design o's recursive discovery out of the cross-category outer loop and into each acquisition run. Across categories, effects cancel: the mean between-category correlation is about 0, and promoted candidates were worth +0.0012 on new seeds against an acceptance threshold of 0.0134. Inside one category the effects are the signal: design q's in-run switches moved job shop by −0.068 to +0.035 and bin packing by +0.004 at sd 0.004. Every held-out run then becomes an independent replicate of the whole recursive process. In each run, design r edits its own score/pick programs, constants and learning principle with o's discoverer (edit-cell weights learned by the current mechanism's own principle, plus a block library). Every candidate gets one round of its learning principle at the same cost, with common random draws. It is judged by the answer the learner would actually give (construction plus the fixed improvement step, capped) on training problems redrawn at each step. A final check on reserved training problems keeps the start unless something learned beats it. The training budget is 400 with n_train 24, and every control is compute-matched. Across categories nothing is searched. The discoverer is amortised instead: edit-cell weights optimised by the chain's principle on pooled in-run values, recurring blocks, and an in-run margin calibrated by retrospective checks. This is a property of the edit space, and its measured differences are large (cell means −0.28 to +0.011). A new generation is adopted only after a paired test on source categories. The likely outcome is partial: a clear test of in-acquisition discovery against compute-matched parameter learning on the four fresh categories, and measurable internal effects of the recursion, but a capability effect of the recursion expected below the detection limit.
why_it_beats_the_measured_limit:
(0) The measured limit. o's confirmation accepts a mean ≥ 0.0134 over 16 (category, seed) pairs at paired sd 0.021 (t ≥ 2.6). Promoted candidates were worth +0.0012 on the confirmation seeds. A real candidate therefore passes with probability about P(Z ≥ 2.6 − 0.0012/0.0053) ≈ 0.01, the same as the null false-acceptance rate of 0.008 to 0.010 per step. Power equals the false-acceptance rate, and 0 of 4 confirmations passed. There are two causes. First, category-specific effects are averaged across categories (fact 1). Second, knapsack (no signal: 0.9069 for every mechanism) and p-median (gain 0) take 79% of o0's CPU per seed (16.3 + 9.2 of 32.3 s).

(1) In-run lineage (one per run). At train 400 and n_train 24 a run has about 9,600 construction-units. One step costs about 610 units:
- one learning round (pop 16 × batch 4) for the parent and for six candidates, 448 units;
- answers on 6 screening problems for all seven and on 6 confirmation problems for the best, about 160 units, with the in-run improvement step capped at 2 constructions.
That gives about 15 steps and 90 candidates per run, more than one o-lineage (about 10 steps and 60 candidates for 6,000 CPU-s). It costs about 2 CPU-s per candidate on a cheap category, against about 100 s per candidate in o.
- Smallest effect accepted in a run: a relative answer-cost gain of at least 0.005 on screening, then at least 0.0025 with at least 4 of 6 wins on confirmation (about +0.002 to +0.004 in score), on one category and undiluted.
- Expected acceptances per run: 1 to 2 real and at most 0.75 false.
- In-run false acceptance: targeted at ≤ 5% per step and measured in development as acceptances whose retrospective check on the reserved problems fails. For comparison, q with a weaker rule switched in 49 of 112 program rounds.
- The final check bounds the loss.

(2) Held-out replicates. Each held-out (category, seed) run replicates the recursive process. o's held-out stage measured one selected mechanism per arm. With 4 categories × 16 seeds and the measured paired sd 0.021 (28 runs of q − o0), se ≈ 0.0026.
- R − O@R ≥ 0.01 with the interval excluding zero needs about +0.015, consistent on at least 3 categories. Power is about 0.25 at the expected +0.005 to +0.01.
- R − Z is detectable only from about +0.007 to +0.008. Power is about 0.15 at the expected +0.003.

(3) Adoption across categories. The discoverer state is estimated from about 1,800 pooled candidate values per generation and chain (20 source runs × 90 candidates). Cell means differ by up to 0.29, so the state is precise. The adoption test uses 5 source categories × 6 new part-B seeds = 30 pairs. It accepts means ≥ 2.6 × 0.021/√30 ≈ 0.010 (0.012 at sd 0.025), with about 1% false acceptance per test (o's noise-only stub, recalibrated for 30 pairs). Expected adoptions per recursive chain over two generations: 0.2 to 0.9, for generation effects of 0.005 to 0.01.

(4) CPU. Source stages need about 75,000 CPU-s. The held-out stage needs about 70,000 on cheap categories and up to 140,000 if one category is expensive. Both fit within 300,000.

The technique replaces a test whose power equals its false-acceptance rate with an in-run test on undiluted per-category effects and a held-out test with run-level replicates. It does not make a recursion effect of +0.003 detectable, and it says so.
recursion:
Within a run (one lineage per run), every accepted mechanism does two things:
- It adds the instruction blocks it inserted, if they are live in it, to the run's library. The splice cells draw from this library in later steps.
- It becomes the source whose init, propose and update programs learn the edit-cell weights from the later steps' candidate values. This is o's rebuild-on-acceptance, now inside the run.
Policy candidates continue a deep copy of the parent's principle state with common draws. So a discovered principle also learns the constants of every later candidate.

Across generations, the reports of generation g's source runs carry every candidate's cells and values, every acceptance with its retrospective check on the reserved problems, the end weights and the live accepted blocks. Generation g+1's starting discoverer is computed from them by registered rules:
- w0 = the weights the chain's principle reaches in 100 iterations maximising Σc pc(w)·μc − 0.01·KL(p(w)‖uniform), where μc is the pooled mean in-run value of cell c, shrunk by nc/(nc+10).
- L0 = live blocks accepted in at least 2 source runs (at most 32).
- m0 = the smallest margin in {0.002, 0.005, 0.01, 0.02} whose pooled retrospective precision is at least 0.6.
- The chain's principle becomes a learning principle accepted in at least 2 source runs with retrospective precision ≥ 0.5, if there is one.

So what generation g discovered sets how generation g+1 generates candidates (w0, L0, and the principle that learns the weights) and how strictly it accepts them (m0). A generation is adopted only if its source runs beat the previous generation's on the confirming half with new seeds: paired mean ≥ 0.005, t ≥ 2.6, CPU ≤ 1.10 times the previous generation's.

Controls that isolate each effect:
- Z (generation 0 on the held-out categories: learned state reset) isolates the cross-generation effect as a whole.
- K (generation 0 plus R1's library only: retains skills but cannot improve its search) separates retained blocks from the improved search (w0, m0).
- F (a chain in which generation 0's principle learns the weights within runs and in amortisation) isolates the role of discovered principles.
- R* (the last amortised state, adopted or not) keeps a contrast even if nothing is adopted.
- O@R and Q@R isolate compute, and search inside acquisition without the discovery machinery.
mechanism_changes:
Not changed: the kernel (run.py, problem.py, environment.py, ledger.py, roles.py), the meter, the references, design_o.py, edits.py and discovery.py. Design r imports them as they are.

New: rsi6/learner/design_r.py.
- Version: {design 'r', o: a design-o mechanism (generation 0: o0), inner: {...}, start: {...}}.
  - inner: kd 6; nedit [0.6, 0.3, 0.1]; cells = the 43 edit cells minus scalar/holdback and scalar/select (the final check is fixed); rounds 1; n_screen 6; n_confirm 6; reserve a quarter of the training problems (at least 3); margin 0.005; wins 4 of 6; ls_cap 2 constructions.
  - start: weights w0 (43 zeros), library L0 (empty), principle source o0, mode recursive or frozen.
- validate, digest, differences.
- class LearnerR(OpenLearner) with:
  - _split.
  - _round: one round of an Acquirer on a batch. Policy candidates take a deep copy of the parent's Acquirer, extended for new constants, so draws on shared coordinates are common (design_o._draw keeps them).
  - _answer_cost: construct + _improve_capped. _improve_capped is learner._improve's default branch (reassign and swap, chain 1, strict), stopped after ls_cap × construction units in-run, or at the test limit's share (2·cu + n² − cu) in the final check.
  - _step: draw six candidates with discovery.Discoverer, then rounds, screening, confirmation, acceptance, D.learn and library update.
  - _final_check: start, parameters-only and final options on the reserved problems, by answer cost. A learned option must beat the start strictly. Each acceptance also gets a retrospective check.
  - _acquire_open.
  - _apply_open: as in design q, the capability's programs and constants, then the unchanged learner._improve.
  - The report holds candidates (cells, values), acceptances (values, retrospective result, blocks), end weights, principle changes, steps and units.
- Untrained answers are o0's, so the gain change and the acquired change coincide against o0-family controls.

New: rsi6/open/discovery_r.py. Pooled statistics from run reports; amortise() (w0 via the chain's principle on the pooled objective, L0, m0, the principle rule); adoption() (paired t over (category, seed)); chain records r_generation and r_adopt.

New: rsi6/open/experiment_r.py. Stages generation1, generation2 and heldout. It is a fork of experiment_q.py: registration and code-hash checks, roles, matched controls via evaluate.raise_until with the design-r run budget, and comparisons via evaluate.compare.

Also new: rsi6/tests/test_design_r.py and rsi6/registry/registration_r.json.

One dispatch line for 'r' (and 'q') goes into rsi6/learner/designs.py. It is added only after registration o's last stage, because that file is pinned by registration_o.json.
measurement_design:
Categories. Development, amortisation and adoption run only on source categories: job shop, quadratic assignment, p-median, knapsack and bin packing. Partitioning and set covering cost 100 to 300 s per run at budget 40, too much at 12×. Held-out: the four fresh categories (single-machine weighted tardiness, unconstrained binary quadratic programming, resource-constrained project scheduling, maximum clique). No run touches them before the held-out stage.

Budgets. Design r runs at train 400, n_train 24, n_fresh 24, test_c 2, test_e 1. Every control uses the same n_train and test budget, with its train raised. Amortisation runs use part A; adoption tests use part B.

Chains.
- R1 and R2: recursive, with independent streams and seeds (two replicates of the cross-category process).
- F: frozen; generation 0's principle learns the weights within runs and in amortisation; uses R1's seeds.
- Each chain runs two generations. Amortisation uses 4 part-A seeds per category per generation (20 runs, about 1,800 candidate values).
- Adoption uses 6 new part-B seeds per test, paired by (category, seed): mean ≥ 0.005, one-sided t ≥ 2.6, CPU ≤ 1.10 times the previous generation's. The false-acceptance rate is measured before registration with o's noise-only stub at 30 pairs.

Held-out arms, paired by (category, seed) on 16 registered seeds H1–H16. The Owner's numbered comparisons are in brackets.
- R: R1's last adopted generation on H1–8 and R2's on H9–16 [1].
- Z: generation 0, H1–16 [4: learned state reset].
- K: generation 0 with R1's library only, H1–8 [3: retains skills].
- F: F's last adopted generation, H1–8.
- R*: the last amortised state of R1 and R2, adopted or not; run only if it differs from R.
- O@R: o0 with train raised pair by pair until its CPU reaches R's (amortisation 4, reading (d); void rules of registration o), H1–16 [5].
- Q@R: q0 raised the same way, H1–8.
- o0@40 and a0@40, H1–8 [2].
- a0@R, paid from the reserve.

Statistic. The registered one: the smaller of the mean changes of the acquired score and of the gain (seeds within category, then categories), with a 5,000-draw bootstrap over categories and seeds. Acquired, untrained, gain and the sign of every category are reported. Internal metrics come from run reports: candidates by cell, steps, acceptances, retrospective precision, principle changes.

Endpoints.
- E1r: R − O@R ≥ 0.01, with the interval excluding zero, not void.
- E2r: R − Q@R and R − a0@40, reported with intervals.
- E3r:
  (a) at least one adopted generation in each recursive chain;
  (b) R − Z > 0 with the interval excluding zero;
  (c) R − K > 0 (point estimate);
  (d) R − F and R* − Z, reported;
  (e) internal: in R, a lower share of candidates from cells with pooled mean below −0.02, and more acceptances per run, than in Z.

Success. "Recursive improvement of capability acquisition observed" only if E1r, E3r(a), E3r(b) and E3r(c) all hold. Anything less is reported as what it is.
predictions: In-run process on held-out runs of R: about 13 to 16 steps and about 90 candidates per run; median 1 in-run acceptance per run (0 to 3); retrospective precision about 0.5 (0.35 to 0.65).

Internal effect of amortisation (E3r(e)): the share of candidates with an edit from a cell whose pooled in-run mean is below −0.02 is about 0.35 in Z and at most 0.15 in R. o's screening put 25% of its edits in such cells. Acceptances per run in R are about 1.5 times Z's (at least 1.3 times).

Parameter learning saturates: O@R − o0@40 ≤ +0.005. To be checked against budget_scaling.json before registration. If o0 gains at least 0.01 more at 200 than at 40 on job shop and quadratic assignment, the next prediction is lowered.
E1r is not met. R − O@R ≈ +0.005 (−0.005 to +0.015); probability that E1r holds about 0.25.
R − Q@R ≈ +0.003 with the interval including zero; R − a0@40 within ±0.02.
E3r(b) is not met. R − Z ≈ +0.003 (−0.003 to +0.008) with the interval including zero; R* − Z about the same.
E3r(c): R − K ≈ +0.001. Retained blocks explain most of what amortisation adds, if it adds anything.

R − F within ±0.003. An in-run change of the learning principle is accepted in fewer than 20% of held-out runs, and no chain's principle changes across generations: the principle recursion is not exercised.
E3r(a): about 0.5 adoptions per recursive chain over two generations; at most one per chain.
At least one held-out category is ceiling-limited for construction policies: every design-r arm equals o0@40 in more than half of its seeds, as on knapsack. Probability about 0.5.
The success condition is not met (probability at least 0.9).
failure_modes: Winner's curse inside the run. What wins on 6 + 6 of the 18 non-reserved training problems does not carry over to fresh instances from other groups. Across seeds, o's candidates fell from +0.0089 to +0.0012. Then R ≈ o0@40 and R − O@R ≤ 0.
Parameter learning is not saturated at 12× (budget_scaling.json may show this). O@R is then a strong control and the advantage of in-run discovery disappears.

Two or more held-out categories carry no signal for construction policies (as on knapsack, 0.9069 for every mechanism, and p-median, gain 0). With two of four categories at exactly zero, 1/16 of the category-bootstrap draws (more than 2.5%) contain only those categories, so E1r and E3r(b) fail whatever the technique does.
In-run false acceptances outpace real ones: q switched in 49 of 112 program rounds, mostly on noise, and single edits average −0.009. Then R < Z < O@R; the final check only bounds the loss.

On binary categories (n_opts 2) the test-time improvement step costs n_vars² units, about 80 constructions on a 250-item knapsack. The in-run evaluation must cap it at 2 constructions and is then only partly aligned with the score, so design r may stay as blind there as o.

CPU. A held-out category as costly as partitioning or set covering (100 to 300 s per run at budget 40) costs 1,200 to 3,600 s per design-r run. The registered halving of its seeds lowers power further.

Negative transfer of the amortised state. Weights learned on five sources suppress cells that pay on a new layout: pick edits are inert on ordered job shop but matter on free-order problems. This shows up as R < Z on a category.
The recursion contrasts are real but below detection (about 0.007 to 0.010, against an expected +0.003): a partial answer, as predicted.
Compute matching fails in some pairs: raise_until does not reach R's CPU, or design r's evaluations cost more CPU per unit than estimated. Those comparisons are void.

The amortised weights mostly encode the pooled cell means, a statistic the experimenter could compute directly. R − Z then measures the value of a learned proposal distribution, not of a deeper recursion.
Operational: designs.py is pinned by registration_o.json. Adding the dispatch before o's held-out stages are recorded stops those stages, so development must use a scratch copy until then.
Development choices (margin grid, n_train 24, train 400, the cap) are tuned on source categories. That is mild meta-overfitting, and only the held-out stage can expose it.
novelty:
No new learning principle is claimed. The parts are known: per-instance algorithm configuration and program search inside a task (racing, genetic programming), learned proposal distributions for search, self-referential learning of the generator (design o's rule), and libraries of discovered blocks (DreamCoder-like).

Relative to design o:
- The recursion moves inside acquisition, so each held-out run tests the recursive process itself. o's held-out stage measures one selected mechanism per arm, and its interval does not cover the spread between runs of discovery.
- Candidate evaluation costs the same for every candidate, is paired with common draws, and is judged by the answer after the improvement step.
- The cross-category loop optimises the discoverer state, not mechanisms, so fact 1 (uncorrelated per-category effects) no longer blocks it.

Relative to design q:
- q searched only score/pick programs, with a fixed inner procedure (the current constants, random 4-problem batches, construction cost, a switch after two batch wins), at budget 40.
- r runs o's full discovery: programs, constants, learning principle, scalars, a discoverer learned by the mechanism's own principle, and a library.
- r gives every candidate a learning round, judges by the answer, and is funded at 12× the units against controls with the same CPU, q@R among them.

What is new is the level at which the recursion is placed and the measurement design, not the components.
implementation_plan:
0. Preconditions. Wait for registration o's last held-out stage (designs.py is hash-pinned), or work on a scratch copy of the package. Read budget_scaling.json when it lands.

1. rsi6/learner/design_r.py, about 500 lines. Reuses design_o.Acquirer, construct, Sensors, compile_vector_program, live and _fitness; learner._key and _finish_arbitrarily; edits.apply_edit and behaviour; discovery.Discoverer.

2. rsi6/tests/test_design_r.py, about 150 lines. Tests:
- _improve_capped equals learner._improve when the meter limit equals the cap;
- no unit is spent outside the meter, and units used ≤ limit;
- the same seed gives the same record;
- when no step is affordable, the capability is o0's start;
- design r's untrained answers equal o0's on the same seed;
- the pinned files are unchanged.

3. Development on source categories only (scratch ledger, development seeds), before any registration.
- D1: job shop and quadratic assignment, 4 seeds (about 1,500 CPU-s). Measure steps, candidates, acceptances, retrospective precision and CPU per run. Choose m0 and the confirmation rule on the registered grid (target precision ≥ 0.5).
- D2: the five source categories, 4 seeds (about 12,000 CPU-s). Generation 0 of r against o0@40, O@R and Q@R on part A, giving per-category effects and paired sd for the predictions and the seed counts. Stop rule: if r − O@R ≤ 0 on every category and the retrospective precision is below 0.3, do not register; report the negative.
- D3: one amortisation on development runs (about 6,000 CPU-s). Internal metrics under amortised against reset weights on two categories.
- D4: null calibration of the adoption rule at 30 pairs with o's noise-only stub (seconds).

4. rsi6/open/discovery_r.py, about 220 lines: pooled statistics, amortise(), adoption(), chain records.

5. rsi6/open/experiment_r.py, about 260 lines, a fork of experiment_q.py: stages generation1, generation2 and heldout.

6. rsi6/registry/registration_r.json with seeds, budgets, rules, endpoints, predictions and file hashes; then the dispatch line in designs.py.

7. Two independent reviews of the code and the registration, as for o; then the registered run.

About 1,100 lines in all, the size of design q with its drivers.
compute_budget:
Basis of the estimates. o0's measured CPU per run at budget 40 is job shop 5.0, quadratic assignment 1.8, p-median 9.2, knapsack 16.3 and bin packing 35.4 s. A design-r run is scaled by about 12: 15 times the training units with the test phase unchanged, and less where the test phase dominates, as on binary categories. A raised control is scaled by about 24, including its lower levels. Design r's evaluations may cost up to 1.5 times more CPU per unit.

Development, before registration, on source categories: about 25,000. This is not part of the 300,000.

Registered, out of 300,000:
- Null calibrations: about 0.
- Generation 1: amortisation runs (3 chains × 5 categories × 4 seeds) about 9,300, plus adoption tests (3 chains × 2 sides × 6 seeds × 5 categories, about 777 s per seed) about 28,000.
- Generation 2: the same, about 37,300.
- Held-out, per cheap category about 17,500, so about 70,000 for four:
  - design-r arms (R 16, Z 16, F 8, K 8 seeds): about 48 runs × 180 s;
  - raised controls (O@R 16, Q@R 8): about 24 × 360 s;
  - references (o0@40, a0@40): about 16 × 15 s.
- A category estimated at more than 600 s per design-r run gets half the seeds. The estimate comes from instance sizes, before any run. This adds up to about 70,000.

Total: about 145,000 to 215,000. The remaining 85,000 or more covers raise_until overruns, R* (about 11,500 if it differs from R) and a0@R (about 11,500). If D2 shows no design-r signal on knapsack and p-median, dropping them from the adoption tests saves about 11,000 per generation.
